definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. When 0 belongs to I this is J_0; the definition does not assume that the different J_i agree.

inputs.statement: n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

For every semiring A satisfying the strong rank condition, every finite index type T, and every family B_t of additive commutative monoids with A-module structures that are free and finitely generated, finrank_A (product over t in T of B_t)=sum over t in T of finrank_A B_t. Here finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (Cardinal.toNat); the strong rank condition means an injective A-linear map A^a to A^b for finite natural a,b implies a<=b.

argument.text: By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

produces.statement: For every i0 in I, J_i0 equals the nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of C, and iota identifies M_R with the direct sum of J e_i0 over i0 in I.

argument.text: Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

produces.statement: T=Q tensor_R J is finite dimensional over Q; mu:T->C, q tensor c |-> qc, is injective; and Q tensor_R M_R is Q-linearly isomorphic to the finite product T^I.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

produces.statement: dim_Q(Q tensor_R J)=1, mu is injective, and the Q-linear span of J in C is one-dimensional.

argument.text: F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

argument.text: Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.
